issues.display_title: Issue #536: Centralize Previous Comment Request Setup
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Previous Comment Request Setup

Summary

Added preparePreviousCommentRequest as a package-local helper and replaced the duplicated setup in the two previous-comment endpoints. Authentication state, pagination, blocked-post validation state, and excluded-user data now come from one implementation without changing either API response.

Changes

  • Added PreviousCommentRequest.go containing:
    • previousCommentRequest
    • preparePreviousCommentRequest
  • Updated ListPreviousComment.go to use the prepared request.
  • Updated ListPreviousReplyComment.go to use the prepared request.
  • Replaced duplicated manual pagination with the existing Functions.Pagination(c, 20) utility.
  • Removed unused context, Redis, and user-function imports from both callers.

Each caller now starts its shared setup with:

request := preparePreviousCommentRequest(c)
if request.unauthorized {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 401, fiber.ErrUnauthorized.Message, "Unauthorized")
}
if request.blockedPost {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 403, fiber.ErrForbidden.Message, "You blocked this post", "blocked")
}

The callers still own the exact HTTP responses. The helper only reports the existing authentication and blocked-post states, avoiding hidden response writes inside request preparation.

Shared Flow

preparePreviousCommentRequest now performs the matching flow once:

  1. Read the current user's encryption identifier.
  2. Retrieve user data and report invalid authentication state.
  3. Read last_login, sid, and commentSid.
  4. Calculate pagination with default limit 20.
  5. Load blocked posts and stop preparation when the target post is blocked.
  6. Load blocked and deactivated users.
  7. Combine those users into notInEncrypt.

Behavior Compatibility

  • Invalid user data still produces the same HTTP 401 response from each caller.
  • A blocked target post still produces the same HTTP 403 response with input blocked.
  • The helper stops before loading user exclusion lists when authentication fails or the post is blocked, matching the previous execution order.
  • Functions.Pagination(c, 20) has the same page, limit, and offset calculation previously duplicated in both files.
  • The previous-comment and previous-reply SQL queries remain in their original endpoints.
  • Query filters, ordering, comment processing, response messages, encryption inputs, and response keys are unchanged.

Scope Audit

  • 1 package-local request helper added.
  • 2 related endpoint callers updated.
  • 100 lines removed from the two callers.
  • 74 lines added across the helper and callers, for a net reduction of 26 lines.
  • No unrelated comment endpoint or response model changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Comments/PreviousCommentRequest.go src/Action/V1/Comments/ListPreviousComment.go src/Action/V1/Comments/ListPreviousReplyComment.go
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Two related comment endpoints repeated the same request preparation flow:

  • ListPreviousComment.go
  • ListPreviousReplyComment.go

Both endpoints retrieved authenticated user data, calculated pagination, loaded blocked posts, rejected a blocked target post, loaded blocked and deactivated users, and combined the excluded user list before running their endpoint-specific queries.

Maintaining this setup in two places could cause access filtering or pagination behavior to drift.

Scope

  • Add one package-local request preparation helper in the Comments package.
  • Reuse the existing global pagination helper with a default limit of 20.
  • Move the matching authentication state, route parameters, blocked-post lookup, and excluded-user lookup into the helper.
  • Update both previous-comment endpoints to consume the prepared request data.
  • Keep each endpoint's comment query, response construction, and encryption logic local.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Retrieval of user data through UserFunctions.UserDatas.
  • The existing HTTP 401 response when user data is invalid.
  • Default page 1 and limit 20 behavior.
  • Redis key names for blocked posts, blocked users, and deactivated users.
  • The existing HTTP 403 blocked-post response and blocked input value.
  • Blocked-user ordering before deactivated-user ordering in notInEncrypt.
  • Existing database queries, ordering, limits, offsets, and error responses.
  • Existing comment transformation and response fields.
  • Existing encrypted and unencrypted response structures.

Out of Scope

  • Updating ListRepliesComment because it also supports viewer access and has a different setup flow.
  • Combining the two endpoint-specific comment queries.
  • Changing comment text fields, including the existing sort_comment key.
  • Changing mobile-facing response schemas or values.
  • Refactoring general user authentication across unrelated APIs.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One package-local helper owns the matching request setup.
  • Both scoped endpoints use the helper.
  • The duplicated Redis and manual pagination setup is removed from both callers.
  • Endpoint-specific queries and responses remain unchanged.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-07. No commit was created.

Implementation: Batch Notification Post Lookup

Summary

Added a package-local batch lookup for notification posts and applied it to both notification-list endpoints. Each endpoint now performs at most one post query and reads post data from a UUID-keyed map while preserving its existing response construction.

Changes

  • Added NotificationPost.go containing:
    • getNotificationPosts
    • notificationPostsByID
  • Updated ListNotifications.go.
  • Updated ListNotificationMonth.go.
  • Added NotificationPost_test.go.

The batch helper retrieves the union of fields required by both callers:

Config.DB.Model(&Models.Post{}).
	Select("id, slug, thumbnail, panorama_quality, post_type, animation, little_planet, pending").
	Where("id IN (?)", postIDs).
	Scan(&posts)

Each response loop now performs an in-memory lookup:

post := postsByID[*notifications[i].PostID]

Behavior Compatibility

  • Notifications remain in the original database order.
  • Nil post IDs are excluded from the batch query and retain their previous response behavior.
  • An empty post-ID list returns an empty map without querying the database.
  • A post ID absent from the query result returns the zero value of Models.NotificationPostQuery, matching the previous empty Scan result.
  • ListNotifications still omits post details when the resolved slug is empty.
  • ListNotificationMonth still applies its existing thumbnail, slug, and pw rules.
  • Panorama decoding and its error response remain in ListNotifications.
  • Post-query failures still return HTTP 500 with Failed to get post data: followed by the database error.
  • No response key, value type, or encryption payload was changed.

Query Impact

Before:

1 notification query + up to N post queries

After:

1 notification query + up to 1 post query

The helper intentionally uses two short in-memory passes: one to collect post IDs and one to index returned posts. This removes repeated database round trips without changing response order.

Test-Driven Verification

TestNotificationPostsByID was added before implementation and initially failed because notificationPostsByID was undefined. After implementation, the test verifies:

  • A returned post is indexed by its UUID.
  • The indexed post retains its data.
  • A missing UUID is not added to the map.

Scope Audit

  • 1 package-local batch query helper added.
  • 1 small post-indexing helper added.
  • 2 per-notification post-query loops replaced.
  • No main notification query, response model, or mobile-facing schema changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Notifications/NotificationPost.go src/Action/V1/Notifications/NotificationPost_test.go src/Action/V1/Notifications/ListNotifications.go src/Action/V1/Notifications/ListNotificationMonth.go
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The focused notification test passes.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Two notification-list endpoints queried the posts table once for every notification containing a post ID:

  • ListNotifications.go
  • ListNotificationMonth.go

A page containing N post-related notifications could therefore execute N additional database queries. Both endpoints used the same post relationship and then attached different subsets of the retrieved post data to their existing responses.

Scope

  • Add one package-local notification post batch helper.
  • Collect non-nil post IDs from the current notification page.
  • Retrieve all matching posts with one IN query.
  • Index the results by post ID for response construction.
  • Update both notification endpoints to use the lookup map.
  • Add a focused test for post indexing and missing-ID behavior.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Notification query filters, visibility rules, ordering, pagination, and totals.
  • Existing handling for notifications without a post ID.
  • Existing handling when a referenced post is missing.
  • ListNotifications post fields and panorama JSON handling.
  • ListNotificationMonth thumbnail and slug behavior.
  • Existing sl, pw, v, and encryption branches.
  • Existing response fields, values, nesting, and types.
  • The existing HTTP 500 post-query error response prefix.

Out of Scope

  • Changing the main notification queries.
  • Changing notification type grouping or visibility rules.
  • Refactoring response construction shared by the two endpoints.
  • Adding caching or parallel database queries.
  • Changing mobile-facing response schemas.

Acceptance Criteria

  • At most one post query runs for each notification page.
  • No post query runs when every notification has a nil post ID.
  • Both scoped endpoints use the shared lookup.
  • No scoped endpoint queries posts from inside its response loop.
  • Returned posts are accessible by their original UUID.
  • Missing post IDs retain the previous zero-value behavior.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-07. No commit was created.

Implementation: Batch Search User Posts

Summary

Replaced the per-user post query in SearchUser with one package-local batch query. The query uses a PostgreSQL window function to preserve the old maximum of four newest posts for each user. Results are grouped by user ID and assigned to the unchanged response model.

Changes

  • Added SearchUserPosts.go containing:
    • searchUserPostRow
    • getSearchUserPosts
    • searchUserPostsQuery
    • groupSearchUserPosts
  • Updated SearchUser.go to collect user IDs once.
  • Reused the same user-ID slice for followed-status and post batch lookups.
  • Removed the post query from the response loop.
  • Added SearchUserPosts_test.go.
  • Kept a code comment explaining why ID collection occurs before response construction.

Batch Query

The new query performs the equivalent of:

SELECT user_id, slug, thumbnail
FROM (
    SELECT user_id, slug, thumbnail,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY user_id
            ORDER BY created_at DESC
        ) AS post_rank
    FROM posts
    WHERE user_id IN (:user_ids)
      AND visibility = 'public'
      AND post_type != 'video360'
      AND is_publish = true
) AS ranked_posts
WHERE post_rank <= 4
ORDER BY user_id, post_rank;

post_rank is an internal query value. It replaces the old LIMIT 4 executed separately for each user and is not selected by the outer query or returned by the API.

Why Per-User Ranking Is Required

A single global LIMIT 4 would return only four posts across all searched users. ROW_NUMBER() restarts numbering for each user_id because of PARTITION BY user_id:

user A: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
user B: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5

Filtering with post_rank <= 4 therefore preserves the previous maximum of four posts for user A and four posts for user B.

Response Compatibility

  • The outer query returns only user_id, slug, and thumbnail; post_rank never reaches the model response.
  • Rows are ordered by user ID and rank before grouping, preserving newest-first order within each user's slice.
  • groupSearchUserPosts initializes every requested user ID with []Models.SearchUserPost{}.
  • Missing posts therefore remain posts: [], not null.
  • The same visibility, post type, publication status, and creation-time ordering are applied.
  • Batch query errors remain non-fatal, matching the previous ignored post-query error behavior.
  • The main search result and followed-status response remain unchanged.

Query Impact

Before:

1 user search query + up to N post queries

After:

1 user search query + up to 1 post query

Test-Driven Verification

The focused tests were added before implementation and initially failed because the batch query and grouping helpers were undefined. After implementation, the tests verify:

  • Post rows are grouped under the correct user ID.
  • Post order is retained during grouping.
  • Users without posts receive a non-nil empty slice.
  • The SQL contains per-user ROW_NUMBER() ranking.
  • The original visibility, post type, and publication filters remain present.
  • The SQL limits results with post_rank <= 4 and orders by rank.

Scope Audit

  • 1 package-local batch post implementation added.
  • 1 per-user post-query loop replaced.
  • SearchUser.go removed 22 lines and added 8 lines.
  • No response model or mobile-facing schema changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Search/SearchUser.go src/Action/V1/Search/SearchUserPosts.go src/Action/V1/Search/SearchUserPosts_test.go
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The focused Search tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

SearchUser queried the posts table separately for every returned user to retrieve that user's four latest public posts. A page containing N users therefore executed N additional post queries.

The existing behavior must still return at most four posts per user, not four posts across the complete search result.

Scope

  • Collect user IDs once from the current search page.
  • Retrieve the matching users' posts with one batch query.
  • Rank posts independently for each user by created_at DESC.
  • Keep only ranks 1 through 4 for every user.
  • Group the query rows by user ID.
  • Assign each grouped post slice to the existing posts response field.
  • Reuse the collected user IDs for the existing followed-status batch lookup.
  • Add focused tests for query rules, grouping, ordering, and empty post slices.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • The main user search query, filters, ordering, limit, and offset.
  • The existing followed-status behavior.
  • Post filters for visibility = public, post_type != video360, and is_publish = true.
  • A maximum of four posts per user.
  • Newest-first post ordering within each user.
  • Existing slug and thumbnail post fields.
  • posts: [] for users without matching posts.
  • Existing post-query failure handling without a new API error response.
  • Every mobile-facing response field and type.

Out of Scope

  • Changing user search ranking or pagination.
  • Changing followed-status queries.
  • Adding new post fields.
  • Filtering banned posts because the previous query did not apply that filter.
  • Returning post_rank in the API response.
  • Changing encryption behavior or response schemas.

Acceptance Criteria

  • SearchUser performs at most one post query for the current user page.
  • No post query runs for an empty user page.
  • The query ranks posts separately with PARTITION BY user_id.
  • post_rank <= 4 reproduces the old per-user LIMIT 4 behavior.
  • Post rows are grouped under the correct user IDs in query order.
  • Users without posts receive a non-nil empty slice.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-07. No commit was created.

issues.display_title: Issue #539: Batch Reply Comment Liked State
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Batch Reply Comment Liked State

Summary

Replaced the per-reply like_comment query in ListRepliesComment with one package-local batch query. The response loop now reads liked state from a map keyed by comment slug.

Changes

  • Added LikedComments.go with:
    • likedCommentSlugsQuery for the user-and-slug batch query.
    • getLikedCommentSlugs for loading liked slugs into a boolean map.
  • Updated ListRepliesComment.go to:
    • Collect reply slugs before response enrichment.
    • Skip liked-state retrieval for viewers and empty reply pages.
    • Execute one batch query for authenticated users.
    • Assign the existing liked field from the lookup map.
  • Added LikedComments_test.go to verify that the query filters by user ID and uses one IN condition for reply slugs.

Query Change

Before:

1 reply-list query + N liked-state queries

After:

1 reply-list query + at most 1 liked-state query

The batch lookup is equivalent to:

SELECT comment_slug
FROM like_comment
WHERE user_id = :user_id
  AND comment_slug IN (:reply_slugs);

Response Compatibility

  • A returned slug is stored as true in likedBySlug.
  • A missing slug reads as the Go map zero value false.
  • Viewers use an empty lookup and therefore continue receiving liked: false.
  • The response field remains named liked and remains a boolean.
  • Reply ordering and all other response fields are unchanged.
  • Database lookup failures retain the existing HTTP 500 response.
  • Encryption output remains unchanged.

Scope Audit

The non-Slim codebase audit found other liked-state checks in PostAgg, ListLikePost, ListLikeComment, CheckLikePost, and V2 DetailPost. Each checks one post or comment per request, so none has the same N+1 pattern.

CommentsSlim.go contains a matching per-reply liked-state query but remains excluded by the requested Slim boundary.

The helper remains package-local because only ListRepliesComment needs a batch comment-slug lookup. Moving it to Utils would add global API surface without reuse.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Comments/ListRepliesComment.go src/Action/V1/Comments/LikedComments.go src/Action/V1/Comments/LikedComments_test.go
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Comments
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The focused Comments tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

ListRepliesComment checked the authenticated user's like_comment row separately for every reply. A page containing N replies therefore executed N additional liked-state queries.

Scope

  • Collect reply slugs from the current page.
  • Retrieve all matching liked reply slugs with one query.
  • Build a lookup keyed by comment slug.
  • Assign each reply's existing liked field from the lookup.
  • Keep the helper inside the Comments package.
  • Add a focused test for the batch query constraints.
  • Audit other non-Slim liked-state queries for the same N+1 pattern.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Reply query filters, ordering, limit, and offset.
  • Reply text unescaping and short/long comment generation.
  • Elasticsearch comment-count lookup and fallback values.
  • liked: true only when the authenticated user liked the reply.
  • liked: false for viewers, missing likes, and empty results.
  • Existing database and Elasticsearch error responses.
  • Encryption behavior and every mobile-facing response field and type.

Out of Scope

  • Changing reply pagination or ordering.
  • Changing comment-count retrieval.
  • Refactoring Slim endpoints.
  • Replacing single-item liked-state queries that do not cause N+1 queries.
  • Creating a global utility for a batch operation with only one caller.
  • Changing response schemas.

Acceptance Criteria

  • ListRepliesComment executes at most one like_comment query for the current reply page.
  • No liked-state query runs for viewers or an empty reply page.
  • The batch query filters by one user ID and all current reply slugs.
  • Every reply retains a boolean liked field.
  • Other non-Slim liked-state usages are audited for matching N+1 behavior.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Implementation: Batch Like-List Followed State

Summary

Replaced per-user CheckFollowed calls in ListLikePost and ListLikeComment with the existing global GetFollowedUserIDs batch utility. Each like-list page now needs at most one follower query.

Changes

ListLikePost.go

  • Collects IDs from []Models.LikedUser before response shaping.
  • Calls UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs once for authenticated users.
  • Reads each user's followed state from map[string]bool.
  • Uses the same map for standard and sl=true responses.

ListLikeComment.go

  • Applies the same batch flow to comment likes.
  • Removes CheckFollowed from the response loop.
  • Keeps the existing standard and sl=true response construction.

Query Impact

Before, per endpoint:

1 like-list query + N followed-state queries

After, per endpoint:

1 like-list query + at most 1 followed-state query

The reused utility performs the equivalent of:

SELECT user_id
FROM followers
WHERE follower_id = :authenticated_user_id
  AND user_id IN (:listed_user_ids);

Why Two Loops Remain

The first loop only collects user IDs required by the batch query. The second loop shapes the existing API response after the followed-state map is available. This prevents a database query inside the response loop while preserving the returned order.

Response Compatibility

  • The original like-list order is unchanged.
  • A user ID returned by the batch query maps to followed: true.
  • A missing ID uses the Go map zero value and remains followed: false.
  • Viewers use an empty map, so every followed state remains false without a query.
  • Standard responses still assign Followed on Models.LikedUser.
  • sl=true responses retain their existing nested users object and sibling followed field.
  • No field names, types, values, or nesting changed.
  • Batch query errors still panic, matching the previous CheckFollowed failure behavior.

Utility Reuse

No new helper was added. UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs already owns the global follower batch lookup and is used by Search and profile follower/following endpoints. The existing followedUserIDSet test covers conversion of returned IDs into boolean lookup values.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Likes/ListLikePost.go src/Action/V1/Likes/ListLikeComment.go
go test -count=1 ./src/Action/V1/Likes ./src/Utils/Functions/UserFunctions
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • Both changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused Likes and UserFunctions tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

ListLikePost and ListLikeComment called UserFunctions.CheckFollowed separately for every user in the returned like list. A page containing N users therefore executed N additional follower queries in each endpoint.

The codebase already provides UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs for retrieving followed states in one batch query.

Scope

  • Collect user IDs from the current post-like page.
  • Collect user IDs from the current comment-like page.
  • Reuse UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs in both endpoints.
  • Build the followed-state map before shaping either response format.
  • Read each user's existing followed value from the map.
  • Keep a code comment explaining why ID collection and response shaping use separate loops.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Like-list queries, filters, ordering, pagination, and totals.
  • followed: true only when the authenticated user follows the listed user.
  • followed: false for viewers and users without a follower row.
  • Standard and sl=true response structures.
  • Post and comment visibility validation.
  • Existing database failure behavior.
  • Encryption behavior and every mobile-facing response field and type.

Out of Scope

  • Changing how likes are created or removed.
  • Changing liked-state checks for the target post or comment.
  • Changing follower relationships.
  • Refactoring dedicated Slim, Worker, or Support files.
  • Creating another helper around the existing global batch utility.
  • Changing response schemas.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Each endpoint executes at most one followed-state query for its current page.
  • The batch query receives all listed user IDs and the authenticated user ID.
  • An empty like page does not execute a follower query.
  • Viewers do not execute a followed-state query.
  • Both response formats retain their existing fields and nesting.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implementation: Batch Elasticsearch Post Counts

Summary

Added ElasticSearch.RetrieveElasticBatch and replaced per-post Elasticsearch GET requests in five post-list flows with one _mget request per page. The utility preserves raw _source JSON and omits missing documents so each caller can retain its original fallback format.

Affected APIs

  • Timeline Recent.
  • Timeline JustForYou.
  • Most Popular Post.
  • Nearest Post.
  • Collection Post Detail.

The first three APIs share enrichTimelinePosts, so their batching is owned by one implementation point in PostResponse.go.

Utility

src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticSearch.go now provides:

func RetrieveElasticBatch(index string, documentIDs []string) (map[string]json.RawMessage, error)

The utility:

  • Returns an empty map immediately for an empty ID slice.
  • Encodes all document IDs into one _mget request body.
  • Reuses the existing Elasticsearch client configuration.
  • Closes the response body after decoding.
  • Maps every found _source to its _id.
  • Omits missing documents instead of returning an error.

The request is equivalent to:

POST /post_<prefix>/_mget
Content-Type: application/json

{"ids":["post_<slug-1>","post_<slug-2>"]}

Timeline Enrichment

PostResponse.go now:

  1. Builds document IDs in the same order as the post slice.
  2. Retrieves all counter sources once.
  3. Looks up each source by its document ID.
  4. Decodes found sources into the existing map[string]interface{} representation.
  5. Passes the unchanged value to applyTimelinePostData.

The obsolete Fiber context parameter was removed from enrichTimelinePosts because Elasticsearch response writing is no longer performed inside that helper. Recent, JustForYou, MostPopular, and the existing empty-list test were updated for the smaller signature.

Nearest and Collection Enrichment

NearestPost and CollectionPostDetail collect document IDs before their response loops. Found sources are wrapped directly in postgres.Jsonb, preserving the previous raw JSON representation.

When a source is missing:

  • NearestPost retains {"counter_view":0,"counter_like":0,"counter_comment":0}.
  • CollectionPostDetail continues using the existing postCount fallback with the same JSON value.

Response Compatibility

  • Posts remain in the database query's original order because the response loops still iterate the original slices.
  • Counter documents are matched by ID, not by Elasticsearch response position.
  • JSON numbers are not converted for raw postgres.Jsonb responses.
  • Timeline sources are decoded into the same map type used by the previous single-document utility.
  • Empty _source objects still trigger the timeline's existing zero-counter default.
  • Missing documents still produce fallback counters instead of an API failure.
  • Description, bookmark, filtering, pagination, encryption, and response schemas remain unchanged.

Query Impact

Before, per affected page:

1 post-list database query + N Elasticsearch GET requests

After:

1 post-list database query + at most 1 Elasticsearch _mget request

Tests

ElasticSearchBatch_test.go uses a local HTTP test server and the real Elasticsearch client transport to verify:

  • The request uses POST /<index>/_mget.
  • The body contains all document IDs.
  • Returned sources are keyed by _id.
  • Empty _source objects are retained.
  • Missing documents are omitted without an error.

The tests were run red before implementation: the initial batch contract failed because RetrieveElasticBatch did not exist, and the missing-document contract failed until fallback behavior was restored.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticSearch.go src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticSearchBatch_test.go src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse.go src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse_test.go src/Action/V1/Posts/NearestPost.go src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostRecent.go src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostJustForYou.go src/Action/V1/Posts/MostPopularPost.go src/Action/V1/CollectionPost/CollectionPostDetail.go
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Several post-list endpoints retrieved Elasticsearch counter documents separately for every returned post. A page containing N posts therefore executed N Elasticsearch requests only to populate post_count.

The affected flows use the same index and document naming convention:

index: post_<prefix>
document ID: post_<slug>

Scope

  • Add a reusable multi-get utility under Utils/ElasticSearch.
  • Retrieve all post counter documents for a page with one Elasticsearch _mget request.
  • Return raw _source JSON keyed by document ID.
  • Update shared timeline enrichment used by Recent, JustForYou, and MostPopular.
  • Update NearestPost.
  • Update CollectionPostDetail.
  • Preserve each endpoint's existing counter representation and missing-document fallback.
  • Add focused tests for request batching, source mapping, and missing documents.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Post-list database queries, filters, ordering, and pagination.
  • post_count field names and JSON types.
  • Existing counter values without numeric conversion.
  • Existing zero-counter fallback when an Elasticsearch document is missing.
  • Description formatting and bookmark state.
  • Collection post JSON field decoding.
  • Existing API error responses for connection, request, or malformed JSON failures.
  • Encryption behavior and every mobile-facing response field.

Out of Scope

  • Changing Elasticsearch index mappings or stored documents.
  • Batching single-post endpoints such as DetailPost, PostAgg, and CounterElastic.
  • Batching comment or folder counter indexes.
  • Refactoring dedicated Slim, Worker, or Support files.
  • Changing response schemas or counter names.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Each affected post-list request performs at most one Elasticsearch counter request.
  • Empty post lists perform no Elasticsearch request.
  • _mget receives all post_<slug> document IDs for the current page.
  • Returned sources are mapped to their original document IDs.
  • Missing documents do not fail the API and retain the previous zero-counter fallback.
  • Timeline post order remains unchanged.
  • Raw Elasticsearch JSON remains raw for NearestPost and CollectionPostDetail.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.
